what_its_for: Pravastatin is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) and fats (triglycerides) in your blood, and to raise good cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart problems. It works best when combined with a heart-healthy diet and regular exercise.
how_to_take: Take pravastatin by mouth with or without food, usually once a day. It is often taken at bedtime, but you can take it at any time of day as long as you take it at the same time every day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 40 mg once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your cholesterol levels and how well you respond to the medication. The maximum dose is typically 80 mg per day. For children and teenagers (ages 8 to 18), doses are lower and determined by the doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pravastatin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice while taking pravastatin, as it may increase the amount of medication in your blood. Limit alcohol, as it can raise your triglyceride levels and increase the risk of liver problems. Avoid starting new medications — including over-the-counter drugs and supplements — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many drugs can interact with pravastatin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark-colored urine, which could be signs of a serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); unusual fatigue or loss of appetite; or memory problems or confusion. Seek emergency help immediately if you think you are having a heart attack or stroke.
when_it_works: Pravastatin starts lowering your cholesterol within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. However, you may not feel any different, because high cholesterol usually has no symptoms. Your doctor will check your cholesterol levels with a blood test after about 4 to 6 weeks to see how well the medication is working. It is important to keep taking it every day, even if you feel fine, because it is working to protect your heart over time.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take pravastatin if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medication and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as muscle problems. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medication may not be right for you. Children: Pravastatin can be used in children ages 8 and older with inherited high cholesterol, under close medical supervision.
